review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

23:1.sourceText: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν τοῖς ὄχλοις καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ
23:1.targetText: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples:

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:2.sourceText: λέγων Ἐπὶ τῆς Μωϋσέως καθέδρας ἐκάθισαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι.
23:2.targetText: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the opening quotation mark.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:3.sourceText: πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε, κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε· λέγουσιν γὰρ καὶ οὐ ποιοῦσιν.
23:3.targetText: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.

groups.note: πάντα ὅσα ἐάν, "all things whatever", is rendered everything.
κατὰ τὰ ἔργα, "according to the works", is rendered what … do.
The prohibition μὴ ποιεῖτε is rendered do not do; μή is not.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί joining "say and do not do" is not expressed; BSB turns λέγουσιν into the clause what they preach.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the relative what when turning "they say" into the object of practice.

23:4.sourceText: δεσμεύουσιν δὲ φορτία βαρέα καὶ ἐπιτιθέασιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αὐτοὶ δὲ τῷ δακτύλῳ αὐτῶν οὐ θέλουσιν κινῆσαι αὐτά.
23:4.targetText: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The possessive αὐτῶν ("their") is not expressed in the English idiom lift a finger.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows the reading φορτία βαρέα καὶ δυσβάστακτα; N1904 lacks καὶ δυσβάστακτα ("and hard to bear").
English supplies the object of lay; the Greek verb ἐπιτιθέασιν has none.
English idiom supplies a verb for the dative τῷ δακτύλῳ ("with their finger").

23:5.sourceText: πάντα δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ποιοῦσιν πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· πλατύνουσιν γὰρ τὰ φυλακτήρια αὐτῶν καὶ μεγαλύνουσιν τὰ κράσπεδα,
23:5.targetText: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.

groups.note: The active ποιοῦσιν ("they do") is rendered in the passive.
The articular infinitive πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι ("in order to be seen") is rendered actively, for men to see.
The article is rendered as the possessive their.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective γάρ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

23:6.sourceText: φιλοῦσιν δὲ τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις καὶ τὰς πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς
23:6.targetText: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is not expressed; BSB lists the items with commas.

23:7.sourceText: καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ καλεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων Ῥαββεί.
23:7.targetText: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.

groups.note: The passive infinitive καλεῖσθαι ("to be called") is rendered as the clause they are addressed.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί is not expressed; BSB continues the list from 23:6 with a comma.
BSB leaves ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ("by men") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English turns "to be called Rabbi" into a noun phrase about the title.
English relative frame for the title; it does not render ὑπό, the agent "by" of men.

23:8.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ κληθῆτε Ῥαββεί· εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ διδάσκαλος, πάντες δὲ ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί ἐστε.
23:8.targetText: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.

groups.note: ἐστιν ὑμῶν, "is of you", is rendered you have.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:9.sourceText: καὶ πατέρα μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος.
23:9.targetText: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.

groups.note: ἐστιν ὑμῶν, "is of you", is rendered you have.
ὁ οὐράνιος, "the heavenly one", is rendered as the clause who is in heaven.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of call that the Greek leaves implied.

23:10.sourceText: μηδὲ κληθῆτε καθηγηταί, ὅτι καθηγητὴς ὑμῶν ἐστιν εἷς ὁ Χριστός.
23:10.targetText: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.

23:11.sourceText: ὁ δὲ μείζων ὑμῶν ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος.
23:11.targetText: The greatest among you shall be your servant.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

23:12.sourceText: Ὅστις δὲ ὑψώσει ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ὅστις ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
23:12.targetText: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

23:13.sourceText: Οὐαὶ δὲ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι κλείετε τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ὑμεῖς γὰρ οὐκ εἰσέρχεσθε, οὐδὲ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἀφίετε εἰσελθεῖν.
23:13.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.

groups.note: ἔμπροσθεν, "before", is rendered in … faces.
The present participle εἰσερχομένους is conative, those trying to enter.
The infinitive εἰσελθεῖν ("to enter") is rendered by in of let in.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the causal ὅτι ("because") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective γάρ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

23:15.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι περιάγετε τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὴν ξηρὰν ποιῆσαι ἕνα προσήλυτον, καὶ ὅταν γένηται, ποιεῖτε αὐτὸν υἱὸν γεέννης διπλότερον ὑμῶν.
23:15.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.

groups.note: The genitive of comparison ὑμῶν ("than you") is rendered as you.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the causal ὅτι ("because") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the predicate (a convert) that γένηται leaves implied.
English supplies the verb of the comparison.

23:16.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοὶ οἱ λέγοντες Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ ναῷ, οὐδέν ἐστιν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ χρυσῷ τοῦ ναοῦ, ὀφείλει.
23:16.targetText: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’

groups.note: The article with the participle, οἱ λέγοντες ("who say"), is rendered as the sentence You say.
ὃς ἄν, "whoever", is rendered If anyone.
ὃς … ἄν, "whoever", is rendered if anyone.
ὀφείλει, "he owes, is obligated", is rendered he is bound.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes explicit what binds him; ὀφείλει has no word for oath.

23:17.sourceText: μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί, τίς γὰρ μείζων ἐστίν, ὁ χρυσὸς ἢ ὁ ναὸς ὁ ἁγιάσας τὸν χρυσόν;
23:17.targetText: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?

groups.note: The article with the participle ἁγιάσας ("that sanctified") is rendered as a relative clause.
τὸν χρυσόν, "the gold", is rendered with the pronoun it.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί is not expressed; BSB combines μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί as You blind fools.
The connective γάρ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

23:18.sourceText: καί Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, οὐδέν ἐστιν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ δώρῳ τῷ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, ὀφείλει.
23:18.targetText: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’

groups.note: ὃς ἄν, "whoever", is rendered If anyone.
ὃς … ἄν, "whoever", is rendered if anyone.
ὀφείλει, "he owes, is obligated", is rendered he is bound.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats the verb of saying from 23:16 (οἱ λέγοντες); the Greek has none here.
English makes explicit what binds him; ὀφείλει has no word for oath.

23:19.sourceText: τυφλοί, τί γὰρ μεῖζον, τὸ δῶρον ἢ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ ἁγιάζον τὸ δῶρον;
23:19.targetText: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?

groups.note: The article with the participle ἁγιάζον is rendered as a relative clause.
τὸ δῶρον, "the gift", is rendered with the pronoun it.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective γάρ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has no verb here.

23:20.sourceText: ὁ οὖν ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ·
23:20.targetText: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.

groups.note: The article with the participle ὀμόσας is rendered he who swears.
πᾶσι τοῖς, "all the things", is rendered everything.

23:21.sourceText: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ ναῷ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ κατοικοῦντι αὐτόν·
23:21.targetText: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.

groups.note: The article with the participle ὀμόσας is rendered he who swears.
The article with the transitive participle κατοικοῦντι ("inhabiting") is rendered the One who dwells in.

23:22.sourceText: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὀμνύει ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
23:22.targetText: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.

groups.note: The article with the participle ὀμόσας is rendered he who swears.
The article with the participle καθημένῳ is rendered the One who sits.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:23.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ ἄνηθον καὶ τὸ κύμινον, καὶ ἀφήκατε τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου, τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὸ ἔλεος καὶ τὴν πίστιν· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ ἀφεῖναι.
23:23.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.

groups.note: The impersonal ἔδει ("it was necessary") is rendered You should have.
μή with the infinitive ἀφεῖναι ("and not to neglect") is rendered without neglecting.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the causal ὅτι ("because") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is not expressed; BSB lists the items with commas.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

23:24.sourceText: ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοί, οἱ διϋλίζοντες τὸν κώνωπα, τὴν δὲ κάμηλον καταπίνοντες.
23:24.targetText: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.

groups.note: The article with the participle, οἱ διϋλίζοντες ("who strain out"), is rendered as the sentence You strain out.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:25.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι καθαρίζετε τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ἐξ ἁρπαγῆς καὶ ἀκρασίας.
23:25.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the causal ὅτι ("because") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:26.sourceText: Φαρισαῖε τυφλέ, καθάρισον πρῶτον τὸ ἐντὸς τοῦ ποτηρίου ἵνα γένηται καὶ τὸ ἐκτὸς αὐτοῦ καθαρόν.
23:26.targetText: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.

unmappedSource.reason: The possessive αὐτοῦ ("of it") is not separately expressed; English says the outside.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows the reading τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος; N1904 lacks καὶ τῆς παροψίδος.

23:27.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι παρομοιάζετε τάφοις κεκονιαμένοις, οἵτινες ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνονται ὡραῖοι, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ὀστέων νεκρῶν καὶ πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας.
23:27.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside, but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.

groups.note: The genitive ὀστέων after γέμουσιν gives full of … bones.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the causal ὅτι ("because") unexpressed.
The particle μέν, answered by δέ (but), has no separate English counterpart.

23:28.sourceText: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνεσθε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δίκαιοι, ἔσωθεν δέ ἐστε μεστοὶ ὑποκρίσεως καὶ ἀνομίας.
23:28.targetText: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί ("also") is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The particle μέν, answered by δέ (but), has no separate English counterpart.
BSB leaves τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ("to people") unexpressed.

23:29.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τοὺς τάφους τῶν προφητῶν καὶ κοσμεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν δικαίων,
23:29.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the causal ὅτι ("because") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:30.sourceText: καὶ λέγετε Εἰ ἤμεθα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, οὐκ ἂν ἤμεθα αὐτῶν κοινωνοὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι τῶν προφητῶν.
23:30.targetText: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’

groups.note: ἄν with the imperfect ἤμεθα marks the unreal past, rendered would have been.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the act implied by "in the blood of the prophets".

23:31.sourceText: ὥστε μαρτυρεῖτε ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν φονευσάντων τοὺς προφήτας.
23:31.targetText: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.

groups.note: The article with the participle φονευσάντων is rendered those who murdered.

23:32.sourceText: καὶ ὑμεῖς πληρώσατε τὸ μέτρον τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν.
23:32.targetText: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.

unmappedSource.reason: The emphatic ὑμεῖς ("you") is not separately expressed with the imperative Fill up.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies what the measure holds; the Greek says "the measure of your fathers".

23:33.sourceText: ὄφεις, γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς φύγητε ἀπὸ τῆς κρίσεως τῆς γεέννης;
23:33.targetText: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?

unmappedSource.reason: English escape takes a direct object, so ἀπό ("from") has no separate counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:34.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω πρὸς ὑμᾶς προφήτας καὶ σοφοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς· ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενεῖτε καὶ σταυρώσετε, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μαστιγώσετε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν καὶ διώξετε ἀπὸ πόλεως εἰς πόλιν·
23:34.targetText: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute in town after town.

groups.note: πρὸς ὑμᾶς, "to you", is rendered as the indirect object you.
The second partitive ἐξ αὐτῶν, "some of them", is rendered others.
ἀπό … εἰς, "from (town) to (town)", is rendered in town after town.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἰδού ("behold") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:35.sourceText: ὅπως ἔλθῃ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς πᾶν αἷμα δίκαιον ἐκχυννόμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος Ἅβελ τοῦ δικαίου ἕως τοῦ αἵματος Ζαχαρίου υἱοῦ Βαραχίου, ὃν ἐφονεύσατε μεταξὺ τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.
23:35.targetText: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:36.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἥξει ταῦτα πάντα ἐπὶ τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην.
23:36.targetText: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:37.sourceText: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν, ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου, ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις ἐπισυνάγει τὰ νοσσία αὐτῆς ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε.
23:37.targetText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀποκτείνουσα is rendered as a relative clause.
The article with the participle ἀπεσταλμένους is rendered those sent.
The prefix of ἐπισυναγαγεῖν ("gather together") gives together.
ὃν τρόπον, "in the way that", is one idiom for as.
The article is rendered as the possessive her.
οὐκ ἠθελήσατε, "you did not want", is rendered you were unwilling.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

23:38.sourceText: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν.
23:38.targetText: Look, your house is left to you desolate.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows the reading with ἔρημος ("desolate"); N1904 lacks it.

23:39.sourceText: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, οὐ μή με ἴδητε ἀπ’ ἄρτι ἕως ἂν εἴπητε Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου.
23:39.targetText: For I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

groups.note: The emphatic double negative οὐ μή is rendered not.
ἀπ’ ἄρτι, "from now on", is rendered again with the negative.
The article with the participle ἐρχόμενος is rendered He who comes.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies that to introduce the statement; the Greek has no ὅτι.
English supplies the copula; the Greek has the participle εὐλογημένος alone.
